body.statement: For every \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}>0\), there exists a sequence \(\{\widetilde C_n^{(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}})}\}\in\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{panel}}_{1-\alpha}(\theta_0,v_0;M,L_0)\) such that \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\mathbb E_{P_{\theta_n(u)}}[\sup_{t\in\mathcal D}\sqrt n\,\operatorname{diam}\widetilde C_n^{(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}})}(v_n(t))]\le L_\alpha(\theta_0,v_0;M,L_0)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\). Conversely, for every generic sequence \(\{\widetilde C_n\}\in\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{panel}}_{1-\alpha}(\theta_0,v_0;M,L_0)\), \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\mathbb E_{P_{\theta_n(u)}}[\sup_{t\in\mathcal D}\sqrt n\,\operatorname{diam}\widetilde C_n(v_n(t))]\ge L_\alpha(\theta_0,v_0;M,L_0)\). There exists a diagonal sequence in this honesty class for which the limit equals \(L_\alpha(\theta_0,v_0;M,L_0)\), and its rules inherit the certified finite upper and lower decision bounds. These quantifiers do not refer to the global projection band \(C_n\), for which no global minimax claim is made.
body.justification: This matching lower bound and attainment theorem is the field-level payoff: it quantifies the exact risk-certificate cost through moving donor constraints.
body.gap: CanenSong2026SimplexWeight proves uniform validity for a fixed optimizer. FreybergerRai2018UniformBands, Definition 1, restricts attention to bands induced by a nonrandom-shape set and rules out random selection among valid bands; Section 2.3 leads with weighted area, and its generic-objective Theorem 2 is accompanied by low-level sufficient conditions and a worked approximation specifically for weighted area. Independently of those results, the unresolved target is the unrestricted externally randomized local max-curve-diameter value and its sharp transfer to a synthetic-control panel.
body.consumer: Software implementing the displayed fixed-ridge quadratic simplex estimator can report how much simultaneous risk uncertainty is information-theoretically unavoidable near the chosen donor-face geometry.
